Claim: PM loop round 5 — `domain:cli` seat.

- Session: `session_01B3Kurx8qufrDzNjk4rag7V` (account `hotlong`)
- Branch: `claude/issue-7652-mcp-capability-substring-match`
- Worktree: dedicated (cloud container)
- Domain: `domain:cli`
- File surface: `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts` (`hasPluginMatching` ~:2327 and the `CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` entries ~:427) + its tests. Stop on breach; explain in the report.
- Container & model: M, `mode:cloud`, `model: claude-opus-5`.
- Serial constraints cleared: **0 in flight in this lane** — all nine of this shift's PRs are MERGED. `serve.ts` was untouched by every one of them (#7914 touched `packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts` and added `packages/cli/test/serve-mcp-stdio-answers.e2e.test.ts`, not `src/commands/serve.ts`). This card was deliberately held behind #7645 for the `packages/mcp` surface; that surface is now free.

### Scope: fix the resolver, not the one collision

The card names the instance (`com.objectstack.connector.mcp` contains `mcp`, satisfies `CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS.mcp.nameMatch`, so `MCPServerPlugin` never loads) **and** the class: *a substring match between a provider plugin name and a consumer plugin name lets a consumer suppress the provider it consumes.* The class is the fix. ⛔ Special-casing the connector's name — an exclusion list, a longer fragment, reordering — leaves the next consumer to rediscover this, and `mcp` is not the only fragment short enough to collide.

⚠️ **Both directions, or it is not a fix.** Tightening the match must not stop a legitimate provider from being recognised: whatever `nameMatch` currently satisfies correctly has to keep satisfying. A resolver that fixes this by matching nothing would make every capability load its default provider and look green in exactly this repro. Pin a provider that *should* match alongside the consumer that should not.

### Pin the consequence

The acceptance criterion is the card's own repro: **on a stock showcase boot, `/api/v1/mcp/skill` answers 200** (and `/mcp` keys `initialize`/`tools/list`) with `ConnectorMcpPlugin` still loaded. ⛔ Not "the resolver returns false for this name" — that pins the mechanism and would pass over a build where the plugin still fails to load for some other reason. The dev proved causality by removal (dropping `ConnectorMcpPlugin` makes MCP work); the fix must make it work **without** dropping it.

### Context worth having, not in scope

This is the third MCP-surface defect this shift: #7645 (stdio transport started but deaf — merged) and #7915 (`os serve` writes its banner to the stdout the stdio transport owns — filed, ungraded). ⛔ Do not fold either in. But if the measurement here turns up something that changes the reading of those, say so in the report.

## ACCEPTED — PR #7935. Landing on gate-green.

Reviewed by the `domain:cli` seat (`hotlong`, session `session_01B3Kurx8qufrDzNjk4rag7V`) against the diff. The ruling was fix-the-class, and that is what landed: `nameMatch` fragments tested with `String.includes()` become `identities` compared by **equality**, and each entry declares the provider's real registered plugin id. ⛔ No exclusion list, no lengthened fragment, no load-order luck — a plugin either is the provider or it is not.

The comment states the general hazard in the form that will actually help the next reader: **a plugin that CONSUMES a capability is conventionally named after the capability it consumes**, so substring matching cannot tell a provider from its consumer — and `mcp` was not the only exposure (`audit` was one consumer away, and every class-name fragment was satisfied by any class merely *ending* in it, e.g. `MyAuditPlugin` for `AuditPlugin`).

### The measurement found something worth more than the fix

Tightening the comparison could have broken legitimate providers, so the identities were **measured against the provider packages instead of assumed** — and that measurement found the registry was already substantially broken:

- **`service-cache` never matched `com.objectstack.service.cache`** — dash versus dot. It has presumably never matched.
- **Eighteen of twenty-three entries were carried entirely by their class name.**

So the "provider already supplied?" check had been running on one working limb for an unknown length of time, and nobody could see it because class-name containment quietly covered for every dead id. That is the kind of thing only a both-directions measurement surfaces; a fix that just special-cased the connector would have left all of it in place.

### Both directions are pinned, and the vacuity traps are closed

The test file states the trap explicitly — *"a resolver that matches nothing would make every capability load its default provider and look green in the repro"* — and pins the negative half accordingly: every registered provider must still satisfy its own capability, by name and by class, across the whole `CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` table, plus a coverage assertion so the expectation table cannot silently fall behind the registry.

Near-misses that substring matching used to accept are pinned as rejections (`com.objectstack.mcp-inspector`, `com.acme.mcp`, `FakeMCPServerPlugin`), as are the degenerate inputs (empty identity list, null-prototype plugin, nameless plugin).

### Two guards I did not ask for and would have wanted

1. **A drift guard for the new brittleness.** Exact ids are precise but rename-fragile, and a provider renaming itself would silently return the resolver to double-loading. The new test **imports each provider package, constructs it, and asserts the name it registers is one the registry declares** — so the fix cannot rot the way the thing it replaced did.
2. **The fixture's consumer identity is pinned against the real connector source.** The e2e declares the consumer inline rather than importing `@objectstack/connector-mcp` (not a `cli` dependency, so `turbo run test`'s `^build` never builds it), which creates an obvious drift risk — the fixture could end up testing a name nobody registers. They closed it by reading `connector-mcp-plugin.ts` and asserting `name = 'com.objectstack.connector.mcp'`. That is the failure mode of their own workaround, found and fenced.

### The acceptance is the real repro, not the mechanism

The e2e boots the **shipped** `bin/run.js` with the consumer plugin loaded and asserts `GET /api/v1/mcp/skill` → **200** and `POST /api/v1/mcp` → real JSON-RPC results for **`initialize`** and **`tools/list`** — the endpoints the card names, with a minted `osk_` key because `/mcp` is authenticated. A `providesCapability(...) === false` assertion would have stayed green on a build where `MCPServerPlugin` fails to load for an unrelated reason; the test file says exactly that and rejects it as the criterion. **Reverse-verified**: restore the substring match and `/mcp/skill` returns to 501.

It also carries a vacuity check — *"the boot really did load the consumer plugin — otherwise this file proves nothing"* — because a fixture that stopped loading the connector would pass for the wrong reason.

### Scope
4 files: `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`, two new tests under `packages/cli/test/`, and the changeset. No `docs/adr/**`, no skills paths, no `content/docs/releases/`.

⛔ Not flipped yet: ESLint and TypeScript Type Check must both read `conclusion: success` on the head commit. ⚠️ Note `packages/cli`'s tsconfig excludes `test/`, so the ratchet may not cover the two new test files — if the job trips anyway, the fix is to type them, ⛔ never to raise the ledger.
